item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: Triangular prism]

Which of these could be folded to make a shape like the 3-D figure above?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles connected in a V-shape by two triangles]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles and two triangles on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles and three triangles]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles, one triangle on the top right and one triangle on the bottom left]

item.figure_description:
The stem shows a 3-D triangular prism resting horizontally on one rectangular face, with dashed lines indicating the three hidden edges. The options show four candidate nets:
- Option A: A central horizontal rectangle with an isosceles triangle attached to each vertical side, and another rectangle attached to the outer edge of each triangle angled upward, forming an open V-shape.
- Option B: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with two identical triangles attached to the right edges of the top and middle rectangles, both pointing right.
- Option C: Two congruent rectangles stacked vertically, each having a triangle attached to its left edge pointing left; a third rectangle extends to the right from the top rectangle, ending with a triangle pointing right.
- Option D: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with one triangle attached to the right edge of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle attached to the left edge of the bottom rectangle pointing left.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

options.label: B

options.label: D

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem shows a net of a cube consisting of six square faces arranged in a cross. A vertical column of four squares has, from top to bottom: a square containing a solid black circle, a square containing an unfilled circle, a square containing a solid black triangle pointing upward, and a blank square. Flanking the second square (with the unfilled circle) are two additional blank squares, one to the left and one to the right.

The options show perspective views of a cube displaying three faces (top, front-left, and front-right):
- A: Top face has a solid black circle, front-left face has an upward-pointing black triangle, and front-right face has an unfilled circle.
- B: Top face has an unfilled circle, front-left face has an upward-pointing black triangle, and front-right face has a solid black circle.
- C: Top face has an unfilled circle, front-left face has a solid black circle, and front-right face is blank.
- D: Top face has an unfilled circle, front-left face is blank, and front-right face is blank.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Figure 1: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom left. The tip of the right-most angle has a line drawn through it. Figure 2: The same triangle, but with the right angle on the bottom right and the angle with the line on the bottom left. Figure 3: The same triangle, but with the right angle facing the bottom left, and the angle with the line on the top left.]

Which of these transformations, taken in order, can be used so that Figure 1 above becomes Figure 2 and then Figure 3?

options.label: A
options.text: reflection and then translation

options.label: B
options.text: reflection and then 1/4 turn rotation clockwise

options.label: C
options.text: 1/2 turn rotation and then translation

options.label: D
options.text: 1/4 turn rotation counterclockwise and then reflection

reference_items.figure_description:
Three right-angled triangles labeled Figure 1, Figure 2, and Figure 3 from left to right:
- Figure 1: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left corner, a horizontal base, and a vertical left side. A vertical line segment connects the hypotenuse to the base near the acute right-most vertex.
- Figure 2: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-right corner, a horizontal base, and a vertical right side. A vertical line segment connects the hypotenuse to the base near the acute left-most vertex.
- Figure 3: A right triangle with the right angle at the bottom-left corner, a shorter horizontal base, and a longer vertical left side. A horizontal line segment connects the vertical left side to the hypotenuse near the acute top vertex.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A trapezoid with two parallel horizontal lines. The right side of the trapezoid is longer than the left hand side.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: An isosceles triangle with the base forming a vertical line.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A parallelogram where top and bottom sides are equal in length and the left and right sides are also equal in length.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes labeled A through D:
A: A trapezoid with horizontal top and bottom parallel sides; the bottom is longer than the top, and the right slanted side is longer and less steep than the left side.
B: An isosceles triangle with a vertical base on the left and a vertex pointing to the right; the top and bottom sides are marked with equal tick marks.
C: A parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides each marked with a single tick mark, and slanted left and right sides each marked with a double tick mark.
D: A scalene right-angled triangle with a vertical left side and a horizontal bottom side, with a right-angle square symbol marked at the lower-left corner.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A person looking at a solid made of cubes]

The solid is made of 5 small cubes.
Which shape does the person in the diagram see?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the middle square]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the right of the middle square]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the middle square and one square attached to the right of the top square]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the top square and one square attached to the right of the middle square]

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top of the item, a person is standing to the left of a three-dimensional solid made of 5 small identical cubes. The person is shown in side profile facing right toward the solid, with a horizontal dotted line extending from the person's eyes to the top-left cube of the solid. The solid is drawn in isometric projection and consists of:
- A central vertical column of 3 cubes.
- One cube attached to the back-right of the top cube of the column, at the same height as the top cube.
- One cube attached to the front-right of the middle cube of the column, extending forward toward the viewer at the middle height level.

The response options each show a flat 2D shape composed of connected unit squares:
- Option A: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square.
- Option B: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.
- Option C: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square and 1 square attached to the right of the top square.
- Option D: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the top square and 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

options.label: B

options.label: C

reference_items.figure_description:
Five squares, labeled A through E, are shown in a row:
- Square A is divided horizontally into 6 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded gray, and the bottom 4 strips are unshaded white.
- Square B has line segments extending from the bottom-left corner to the center, from the bottom-right corner to the center, and from the center to the top-right corner. The triangle formed at the bottom is white, and the remaining area of the square is shaded gray.
- Square C is divided vertically into three regions by two vertical lines: two narrow gray strips on the left and right edges, each approximately one-sixth the width of the square, and a wider unshaded white region in the middle.
- Square D contains an unshaded white isosceles triangle whose base is the bottom edge of the square and whose apex touches the midpoint of the top edge. The two right-triangular regions to the left and right of this triangle are shaded gray.
- Square E is divided vertically into 3 strips of equal width. The leftmost and rightmost strips are shaded gray, and the middle strip is unshaded white.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A rectangular prism, with a length of 5 blocks, width of 4 blocks, and height of 3 blocks. There is a hole shown on the top of the rectangular prism. The hole is 2 blocks by 3 blocks and goes all the way through the shape.]

The figure above shows a shape made up of cubes that are all the same size. There is a hole all the way through the shape. How many cubes would be needed to fill the hole?
reference_items.figure_description: An isometric drawing of a 3D block shape constructed from identical unit cubes. The overall block is 5 cubes wide along the front, 4 cubes deep along the right side, and 3 cubes tall. In the center of the top face, there is a rectangular rectangular hole measuring 3 cubes wide by 2 cubes deep, bordered by a rim that is 1 cube wide on all four sides. The hole extends vertically straight down through the entire height of 3 cubes.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
